title: The 10 Best Biscuit Joiners
subtitle: Corded and cordless biscuit (plate) joiners for tabletops, cabinets and frames, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A biscuit joiner cuts slots for glued wooden biscuits that align and strengthen joints in tabletops, cabinets and frames. We ranked 10 best-sellers from DEWALT, Makita, Lamello, WEN and budget brands on rating, review volume and features (a rack-and-pinion fence, an angle fence, dust collection, cordless power and biscuits in the box).

changelog.note: Replaced the PORTER-CABLE 557, which no longer has a seller on Amazon, with the Lamello Zeta P2 ($2,175), which takes the Money No Object badge. The Ecarke DEWALT-battery joiner we warned against is no longer sold; the new pick to avoid is Ecarke's Makita-battery version. Prices and ratings re-checked.
Prices, ratings and review counts re-checked on 9 of 11 listings. Biggest price moves: the VEVOR M1K-ZK5-100 rose from $52.11 to $69.90; the WOODSTARTER 458618261 rose from $59.99 to $64.99.
Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

avoid.name: Ecarke Cordless Biscuit Joiner Compatible with Makita 18V Battery, Tool Only
avoid.flag: Claims 0-90° cutting with a fixed fence
avoid.verdict: A Makita-battery joiner whose listing contradicts itself on the fence, and it has the lowest rating of the joiners we looked at.
reasons: The title and bullets promise 0-90° cutting, but another bullet describes a fixed fence ('fixed baffle') with an auxiliary module for offset, so it's unclear what actually adjusts.
The listing gives two different model numbers (part number BGSZ011T0A1, model number FPCAG 001).
It's a third-party body on Makita batteries, so Makita doesn't warrant it. Makita owners can buy the XJP03Z, with a rack-and-pinion fence and 4.8 stars.
It's rated 3.7 stars, the lowest of the joiners we looked at.

buyers_guide.q: What does a biscuit joiner do?
buyers_guide.a: It cuts matching crescent slots in two boards. You glue in a compressed wooden biscuit, which swells and locks the joint and keeps edges aligned. It's fast for tabletops, cabinet carcasses and face frames.
#0, #10 and #20 cover most work; use the largest that fits the board. Most joiners have preset stops for all three.
The fence sets how far the slot is from the face. A rack-and-pinion fence stays parallel to the blade, so slots line up on both boards. A tilting fence handles mitered corners.
Corded is cheaper and has unlimited runtime. Cordless DEWALT and Makita joiners are handy for site work and assembly in place.
Biscuits are quickest and forgiving for alignment. Dowels and Festool Domino tenons are stronger for chairs and frames under heavy load.
